Ivy (People Ops): Heads up for managers running promos this quarter 1: a few nuanced Qs on eligibility, comms, and legal checks so posting answers here.
Marcus (Eng Manager): First: someone hit a big client milestone but joined 3 weeks ago. Are they eligible for a promo this cycle?
Bea (People Ops Partner): Eligibility baseline: 90 days in role is preferred, but exceptions allowed for demonstrable impact + manager endorsement. if <90 days, include a short exception rationale and loop in @Bea and @Lena for final sign-off.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Got it. Second: we want to do a quiet title change without public announcement due to sensitivity. Any policy we should follow?
Lena (Legal): Quiet title changes are fine, but ensure offer letters, employment agreements, and comp records are updated prior to any external-facing announcement. also check for contractual notification obligations in customer contracts if title affects delivery terms.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Thanks. Third: can we announce internal promos at team all-hands before payroll reflects comp change?
Ivy (People Ops): Best practice: wait until comp-change is submitted in the system and manager-notification step is complete. title-only announcements can go after manager-notify. if comp is pending payroll processing, phrase comms as "pending admin processing" to avoid confusion.
Omar (Payroll): Note: if an announcement causes inquiries about pay timing, point folks to payroll cutoffs. for July payroll the approved comp-change must be in by 2025-07-08 17:00 PT. retro-pay takes 1-2 cycles.
Marcus (Eng Manager): What about managers who want to cascade promotions with equity grants simultaneously?
Bea (People Ops Partner): Equity grants are handled by Talent & Compensation. include the equity request ticket alongside the comp-change form. do not promise equity to an employee verbally until Talent confirms grant approvals.
Marcus (Eng Manager): If a promoted IC is on a performance improvement plan (PIP), can we still promote?
Lena (Legal): Promotions while on PIP are unusual. consult People Ops + Legal; we require documented rationale and review of any performance-related clauses. promotions can't be used to circumvent performance processes.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Evidence question: managers have noisy artifacts (many PRs). what should we attach?
Ivy (People Ops): Attach 2-3 artifacts that best demonstrate sustained impact and the manager's written summary. one-line captions for each artifact help reviewers. avoid attaching full meeting recordings unless clipped to the key segment and timecode.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Appeals: if employee contests outcome after manager notification, what's the timeline and what's reviewed?
Bea (People Ops Partner): Appeal window is 14 days from manager notification. panel reviews new evidence only; re-arguing the same items rarely changes outcomes. final decision shared within 10 business days of appeal filing.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder scheduled: "Promo eligibility Q&A recap posted" on 2025-06-20 09:00 PT.
Ivy (People Ops): I'll publish a 1-pager (eligibility, comms checklist, legal touchpoints) to #people-ops-resources and tag managers. ping @Bea for exceptions or if you need a sample comms script.
Marcus (Eng Manager): Perfect, appreciate it 44d
Lena (Legal): If anyone has international-specific employment law questions, DM Legal with country and employment details before making commitments.
Omar (Payroll): And loop payroll early if promos overlap with cross-border payroll runs. we've seen timing snafus otherwise.
Ivy (People Ops): Thanks team 64f — closing thread and will post materials.
